account-requirement-sub: CoPo forwards requests through your own Copilot license. {plansLink}.
account-unauth-body: Sign in with the GitHub account that holds your Copilot subscription. Until you do, the proxy accepts connections but rejects Copilot calls.
account-pending-body: We’ll copy your sign-in code and open GitHub for you. Paste the code on the GitHub page to finish.
account-roster-sub: Other accounts saved on this {os, select, macos {Mac} other {computer}}. Switching restarts the proxy signed in as that account.
account-switch-different: Sign in as a different account
account-rosters-divider: or use an account you already know
account-remembered-sub: Accounts you’ve signed into before on this {os, select, macos {Mac} other {computer}}. Picking one restarts the proxy signed in as that account.
account-gh-reuse-sub: Sign in with an account you’re already logged into with {ghCode} on this {os, select, macos {Mac} other {computer}} — no code to copy.
account-confirm-sign-out: Sign out? The proxy will restart and stop forwarding Copilot requests until you sign in again.
account-confirm-remove: Remove {login}? CoPo forgets its saved sign-in. This doesn’t sign you out of gh or GitHub in the browser.
account-err-gh-use-generic: Couldn’t sign in with that account. Try the code-based sign-in above.
account-err-gh-use-authless: Signed in as {login}, but the proxy came back unauthenticated — that account may not have Copilot access on this host.
account-err-gh-use-no-restart: Sign-in didn’t complete — the proxy may not have restarted. Try again, or use the code-based sign-in above.
account-err-switch-authless: Switched, but the proxy came back unauthenticated — that account’s token may no longer be valid.
account-err-switch-no-restart: Switch didn’t complete — the proxy may not have restarted. Try again.
account-rejection-explain-402: Check your Copilot plan or billing on GitHub, then try again.
account-rejection-explain-403: This model or request isn’t allowed on your current plan.
account-rejection-explain-timeout: It took too long to respond. Try again in a moment.
account-rejection-explain-429: You’ve hit a rate or quota limit. Wait a moment and try again.
account-rejection-explain-5xx: GitHub’s side returned an error. This is usually temporary — try again shortly.
account-rejection-explain-other: Try again, or check your Copilot account on GitHub.
apps-sub: Configure your tools to use CoPo. We’ll check for each app before setting it up.
endpoint-sub: Where CoPo listens. Use these values when wiring up a tool that isn’t in the Apps list.
endpoint-hint: The key rotates every time CoPo restarts. Use {apiKeysLink} to mint a stable, named key for long-running tools.
keys-sub: Keys that apps use to call CoPo. Add one per tool so you can tell them apart — anything not listed still works by default.
models-sub: Models available to apps through CoPo, grouped by kind. The list is fetched from the provider — refresh to pull the current catalog if a model looks missing.
logs-sub: Daily-rotated request and handler logs, {n, plural, one {#-day} other {#-day}} retention.
logs-where-hint: Each handler writes a per-day file under the maximal state directory. Reveal the folder to inspect them, or tail the active file with {tailCmd}.
logs-retention-value: {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, then deleted on next boot
diagnostics-sub: Live state and a one-click bundle for bug reports.
diagnostics-copilot-refresh: Token will refresh on first request
uninstall-hint: This stops CoPo’s background agent, reverts any app integrations, and removes the {cliName} CLI from your PATH. You’ll drag CoPo to the Trash to finish.
uninstall-confirm:
Uninstall CoPo?

This stops the background agent and {summary}. You’ll drag the app to the Trash to finish.

This can’t be undone.
uninstall-err: Couldn’t finish uninstalling: {error}. You can run {uninstallCmd} in the terminal instead.
uninstall-complete: CoPo is uninstalled. Quit CoPo from the {os, select, macos {menu bar} other {system tray}}, then drag it from Applications to the Trash to finish.
dashboard-events-meta: Page {page} / {total} · {events, plural, one {# event} other {# events}}
dashboard-empty-summary: No token usage recorded for the selected period.
dashboard-empty-events: No token usage detail rows for the selected period.
dashboard-welcome-body: Usage and token-usage data will appear here as it loads.
native-notify-startup-body-macos: Look for the CoPo icon in your menu bar ↑
native-notify-startup-body-other: CoPo is running in your system tray ↓
native-notify-signin-body: CoPo needs your GitHub Copilot account before it can serve requests. Click here — or the menu-bar icon — to open Settings and sign in.
native-notify-failed-body: The background proxy failed to start. Click the menu-bar icon to retry startup or view the logs.
native-notify-failed-body-reason: {reason} — click the menu-bar icon to retry startup or view the logs.
native-notify-rejection-body: An upstream Copilot request was rejected. Open Settings for details.
native-quit-body: CoPo will stop and any open Settings windows will close.
activity-hint: Request activity through CoPo since its last restart. Finished means the last request completed; it does not mean the app’s entire task is done. Stopped means a request failed or was interrupted.
activity-active: {n, plural, one {# active request} other {# active requests}}
companion-recovery-help: Your tools are not reachable. Retry startup or open the logs for details.
companion-verify-help: Send a request through this connection to verify it.
companion-empty: Connect a tool to get started.
companion-signin-help: Sign in with GitHub to connect your tools.
companion-cat-label: CoPo Companion: {status}. Click to open your tools.
companion-action-error: The action could not be completed. Please try again.
companion-account-busy: Wait for running requests to finish before managing accounts.
personalization-sub: A little companion, on your terms.
personalization-save-error: Could not save preferences. Please try again.
personalization-desktop-only: Open CoPo’s desktop app to change these preferences.
companion-upstream-help: The upstream service reported a problem. Open Account for details and recovery.
connection-error-base-url: Claude Code is configured for another gateway. Remove ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL from its settings, then try connecting again.
connection-error-helper: Claude Code uses a custom API key helper. Remove apiKeyHelper from its settings, then try connecting again.
connection-error-api-key: Create an enabled API key in CoPo Settings, then try connecting again.
connection-error-install: Install Claude Code, then try connecting again.
connection-error-gateway: CoPo could not reach the gateway. Reopen CoPo and try again.
apps-configured-missing: Configuration saved, but the app could not be found.
apps-configuration-error: Could not change the configuration. Check that CoPo is running, then try again.
apps-conflict-detail: {name} already has a custom {setting}. Remove that setting from the app’s configuration, then choose Configure again.
apps-install-missing: CoPo couldn’t find {name} on this computer.
apps-install-command-help: {os, select, windows {Open PowerShell and run this command to install {name}.} other {Open Terminal and run this command to install {name}.}}
apps-copy-manually: Couldn’t copy automatically. Select the command above and copy it manually.
apps-install-desktop-help: {os, select, linux {Claude Desktop is available for macOS and Windows. See the official download page for supported systems.} other {Download Claude Desktop from the official website, install it, and open it once.}}
apps-open-download-error: Couldn’t open your browser. Open {url} manually.
apps-install-generic: Install {name} from its official website, then return here.
apps-check-again-help: When installation is complete, choose Check again to detect and configure the app.
apps-restart-help: On Windows, a running Claude Code session keeps using CoPo until you restart it.
apps-restart-command: After disconnecting, run {command} in Claude Code and start it again for the change to take effect.
apps-codex-existing: Your existing Codex setup already uses CoPo. Configure adds separate CoPo settings; Disconnect restores your existing setup.
